# Dimension-free approximate classicalization for pure-state families

## Theorem

Let $H$ be any finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\mathcal F$ be an arbitrary (possibly infinite) family of pure states $P_\psi=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ on $H$, and let
\[
\mathcal B:\mathcal T(H)\longrightarrow\mathcal T(H\otimes H)
\]
be a channel. Write $\mathcal B_a$ for its $a$th output marginal. Suppose, uniformly for every $P_\psi\in\mathcal F$,
\[
T(\mathcal B_a(P_\psi),P_\psi)\le b,\qquad a=1,2,
\]
where $T(\rho,\sigma)=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$. Then there is an entanglement-breaking channel $\Lambda:H\to H$ such that
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal F}T(\Lambda(P),P)\le f(b),
\]
with the dimension- and family-independent modulus
\[
\delta=4\sqrt b,\qquad
\eta=\frac32\left((1-4\delta)^{-1/2}-1\right),
\]
\[
f(b)=
\begin{cases}
\min\{1,\delta+\eta+\sqrt{2\eta}\},&0\le b\le 1/4096,\\
1,&b>1/4096.
\end{cases}
\]
In particular, $f(0)=0$ and $f(b)=O(b^{1/4})$ as $b\downarrow0$ (indeed $f(b)\sim2\sqrt6\,b^{1/4}$). No unitality or bistochasticity assumption is made on $\mathcal B$.

The proof is uniform in $\dim H$, the cardinality of $\mathcal F$, and all priors. Finite dimensionality is used for the final compactness/minimax step.

## Proof

### 1. Uniform Stinespring-vector comparison gives a cb Schur bound

First fix an arbitrary finite list $\{P_i=|\psi_i\rangle\langle\psi_i|\}_{i=1}^n\subseteq\mathcal F$. Take a Stinespring isometry
\[
V:H\longrightarrow H\otimes H\otimes E
\]
for $\mathcal B$, and put $u_i=V\psi_i$. Since the trace distance to a pure target bounds the probability of the complementary two-outcome test,
\[
\langle u_i|(P_i\otimes I)|u_i\rangle\ge1-b,
\qquad
\langle u_i|(I\otimes P_i)|u_i\rangle\ge1-b.
\]
The two projectors commute and
\[
I-P_i\otimes P_i\le (I-P_i)\otimes I+I\otimes(I-P_i),
\]
so
\[
q_i:=\langle u_i|(P_i\otimes P_i\otimes I_E)|u_i\rangle\ge1-2b.
\]
For $b\le1/4096<1/2$, project $u_i$ onto $\psi_i\otimes\psi_i\otimes E$ and normalize the environment component to a unit vector $e_i\in E$, choosing its phase so that
\[
v_i:=\psi_i\otimes\psi_i\otimes e_i
\quad\hbox{satisfies}\quad
\langle v_i,u_i\rangle=\sqrt{q_i}\ge0.
\]
Then
\[
\|u_i-v_i\|^2=2(1-\sqrt{q_i})
\le2(1-\sqrt{1-2b})\le4b,
\]
hence $\sup_i\|u_i-v_i\|\le2\sqrt b$.

# Audit: pure-family classicalization in separable infinite dimension

## Verdict

The proposed Stinespring-continuity extension is sound, conditional on the finite/algebraic core already stated: for the partition matrix \(Q\), assume

\[
\|S_C-S_{CQ}\|_{cb}\le a<1,
\qquad |C_{ij}|\ge 1-\eta\quad(i\sim_Q j).
\]

Here \(C_{ij}=\langle\psi_i,\psi_j\rangle\) is the Gram matrix of unit vectors in a separable Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), and \(Q_{ij}=1\) within each equivalence block and \(0\) between blocks. For the constants in the stated finite proof, \(a=\delta+\eta\), \(\eta=\tfrac32[(1-4\delta)^{-1/2}-1]\), and \(\delta\le1/16\), so \(a\le \sqrt3-\tfrac{23}{16}\approx0.2946<1\).

For \(b>0\), the construction below gives a normal entanglement-breaking CPTP map \(\mathcal E_*:\mathcal T(\mathcal H)\to\mathcal T(\mathcal H)\), whose dual \(\mathcal E:B(\mathcal H)\to B(\mathcal H)\) is normal UCP, satisfying

\[
\sup_i \tfrac12\|\mathcal E_*(|\psi_i\rangle\langle\psi_i|)-|\psi_i\rangle\langle\psi_i|\|_1
\le \min\{1,\ a+\sqrt{2\eta}\}.
\]

This is at least as strong as the suggested safe estimate \(2a+\sqrt{2\eta}\). If \(b=0\), then \(a=\eta=0\) and the same argument gives exact classicalization.

## 1. The exact KSW theorem that applies

Use Kretschmann–Schlingemann–Werner, *A Continuity Theorem for Stinespring’s Dilation*, arXiv:0710.2495 (published J. Funct. Anal. 255 (2008), 1889–1904). Theorem 1 states: for completely positive maps \(T_1,T_2:A\to B(K)\), with \(A\) any C*-algebra and at least one map nonzero, their Bures/Stinespring distance satisfies the following bound. Our unital Schur channels meet the nonzero condition.

\[
\frac{\|T_1-T_2\|_{cb}}{\sqrt{\|T_1\|_{cb}}+\sqrt{\|T_2\|_{cb}}}
\le \beta(T_1,T_2)\le \sqrt{\|T_1-T_2\|_{cb}},
\]

and there is a common representation \(\pi:A\to B(L)\) and corresponding Stinespring operators \(V_1,V_2:K\to L\) attaining

\[
\|V_1-V_2\|=\beta(T_1,T_2).
\]
The theorem permits \(\pi\) to be the direct sum of the two minimal Stinespring representations. Its statement places no finite-dimensional or separability hypothesis on \(A\) or \(K\). In particular, it applies to \(A=B(\ell^2(I))\), even if the index set \(I\) is uncountable and \(\ell^2(I)\) is nonseparable.
